name: Moreeb Dune (Tal Moreeb)
distance: About 3 hours from Abu Dhabi city (sources give roughly 220 to 250km); guides put Dubai at about 3.5 to 4 hours
desc: A very large sand dune south of the Liwa villages, usually quoted at around 300m high with a slipface of about 50 degrees. A paved road reaches its base; the sand itself is for 4x4s and the annual hill climb.
bestTime: October to April, with the festival season from December the busiest. Go early in the morning, when the sand is cooler; one guide says it holds heat from midday.
timeNeeded: A full day from Abu Dhabi or Dubai: about three hours each way by road, plus an hour or two at the dune. An overnight stay suits those who want to see it in both morning and evening light.
fees: The official festival site says general admission to the festival grounds is free, with separate fees for some competitions and VIP areas. No entry fee for the dune itself outside the festival is published.
hours: No opening hours for the dune outside the festival are published. During the festival, the Liwa Sports Club app is the official place for schedules.

access.note: A paved, double-lane road is reported to run all the way to the dune's base, so an ordinary car can reach it. A 4x4 is needed only to drive on the sand, and one reviewer notes that sand sometimes covers parts of the tarmac. One guide describes unpaved tracks and says a 4x4 is essential for the final stretch, but most sources report tarmac all the way to the base.

facilities.note: Reviewers on Tripadvisor report large car parks, a park with WCs and a children's playground opposite the dune, and cafeterias that open only during events; the official festival site says amenities are limited in remote areas and that mobile service may be weak. Shade, fuel at the base and facility opening hours are unconfirmed, so bring food, water and shade.

gpsSource: Wikipedia's Moreeb Dune infobox gives 22.97966667, 53.78622222 (read through the Wikipedia API). Wikimedia Commons photos of the dune carry nearby geotags (22.979578, 53.786269 and 22.976697, 53.7915). Wikipedia does not say whether the point is the crest or the base, so treat it as a point on the dune and confirm on the ground. A third-party guide lists 22.971, 53.774, which was not used.
body:
Moreeb Dune, also written Tal Moreeb (تل مرعب), is a large sand dune in the Empty Quarter desert, in Abu Dhabi's Al Dhafra region. It lies south of the Liwa villages. The height is usually quoted at around 300 metres (Visit Abu Dhabi says over 300), but measured figures run nearer 220 metres: PeakVisor lists 223 metres above sea level, and one Tripadvisor reviewer measured 209 metres on Google Earth. The 50-degree figure is the slipface, not the whole climb, and the length is about 1,600 metres.

The road is the easy part. Guides describe a fully paved, double-lane road running all the way to the dune's base and the festival site, so an ordinary car can park and a visitor can walk up. Driving on the sand is another matter. The official festival site recommends a 4x4 for dune exploration and says the main landmarks can be reached by paved road without one. A booking-site guide to the dune lists three ways up: on foot (30 to 60 minutes and physically demanding, by its estimate), by quad bike or buggy, or in a 4x4 with an experienced driver.

The dune is best known for the Liwa International Festival and its hill climb, where four-wheel drives, quad bikes and dirt bikes race up the face. Wikipedia traces the event to 2001, when local Emiratis began competing on the dunes, and says an official festival began in 2004 under what became the Liwa Sports Club. The most recent edition ran from 12 December 2025 to 3 January 2026, and organisers reported more than 700,000 visitors. Outside the festival, the dune is an open stretch of sand with limited services.

This page covers the dune. For the wider oasis, its date farms and its history, see our Liwa Oasis guide.

guide.gettingThere: From Abu Dhabi city the official festival site says Liwa takes about 3 hours and gives the route as Sheikh Zayed Road (E10) towards Sweihan and Al Ain, following signs for Liwa. Other guides describe the E11 and E45 via Madinat Zayed and put the distance at about 220km, while Wikipedia says about 250km to the dune; the figures differ, so allow about three hours. From Dubai, no official figure was found: one guide says about 3.5 hours and another about 4 hours, and one gives about 350km. The final road is reported to be paved to the dune's base and the festival site, so any ordinary car can make the journey; the official site says taxis run from Abu Dhabi, though a round trip by taxi was not priced in any source. A guide that lists the nearest supermarkets names Madinat Zayed, so stock up there or in Abu Dhabi, as fuel and shops at the dune are unconfirmed.
guide.whenToGo: The official festival site recommends October to April, when cooler temperatures suit outdoor activity. One guide gives 22 to 30°C for those months, and another calls November to March the peak. The Liwa International Festival is the busiest period. The 2025–26 festival ran from 12 December 2025 to 3 January 2026, and the Moreeb Dune Car Championship, with its races and hill climbs, was reported by Gulf News for 31 December 2025 to 3 January 2026. For 2026–27 the official festival site (checked 1 October 2026) and Khaleej Times give 11 December 2026 to 2 January 2027; the hill-climb dates for that edition had not been published. Visit Abu Dhabi says the hill climb is typically in late December. Check the Liwa Sports Club app for the schedule before you plan around it.
guide.onSite: Visitors can walk up the dune and watch vehicles on it. Tripadvisor reviewers describe a park with WCs and a playground opposite the dune and large car parks, with cafeterias operating during events only, and facilities may be busier or closed outside the festival. During the festival, the grounds include areas for motorsport, dining, a heritage village and camping, with a ferris wheel and hot-air balloon rides reported by Gulf News. The Desert Safaris Booking guide says climbing on foot takes 30 to 60 minutes and is physically demanding; it advises closed shoes. The official site recommends a 4x4 for dune exploration, and the Desert Safaris Booking guide lists a 4x4 with an experienced driver as one way up.
guide.safety: Heat is the main hazard. The official site warns of extreme daytime heat and cold nights, and advises layers, sunscreen, sunglasses, a hat and plenty of water. One blogger reports that the sand can burn bare feet, and the Desert Safaris Booking guide says it holds heat by midday, so go early and wear closed shoes. A Tripadvisor reviewer says you need a hat by mid-morning. The official site recommends a 4x4 for dune exploration, says camping is safe with proper preparation and recommends guides. Mobile coverage may be weak away from the main areas, so a downloaded offline map is sensible.
guide.heritage: Wikipedia dates the festival to 2001, when local Emiratis began competing by climbing dunes with bikes and cars, and to 2004, when the Abu Dhabi government set up a motors club that later became the Liwa Sports Club and launched the first official festival. Visit Abu Dhabi calls the Moreeb Hill Climb a motorsport event within the Liwa International Festival. Wikipedia calls the dune one of the largest hill climbs in the world.
guide.etiquette: The official festival site says camping is safe with proper preparation and recommends guides, and names the Liwa Sports Club for campsite booking. Gulf News says the festival venue has designated camping sites; use those or a booked camp.

glance.how: Paved road to the base; the sand needs a 4x4
glance.time: A full day from Abu Dhabi or Dubai
glance.cost: Festival grounds free; some events charged

quick: In Al Dhafra, south of the Liwa villages, at the northern edge of the Empty Quarter.
Usually quoted at around 300 m; measured figures run nearer 220 m (PeakVisor lists 223 m above sea level). The slipface is about 50 degrees.
About 3 hours from Abu Dhabi city (220 to 250km depending on the source). Guides put Dubai at about 3.5 to 4 hours.
Not to reach the base: a paved road is reported to run to it. You do need a 4x4, ideally with a guide, to drive on the sand.
It runs within the Liwa International Festival, which the official site lists as 11 December 2026 to 2 January 2027 (checked 1 October 2026). Hill-climb dates for that edition were not yet announced.
Reviewers report car parks, a park with WCs and a playground, and cafeterias during events. Bring food, water and shade.

The festival area and the nearby desert are used for camping in season, through the Liwa Sports Club or at nearby resorts. Visit Abu Dhabi advises against pitching at the foot of large dunes. One blogger reports wild camping off an unpaved road, but no official rule is published.

faqs.a: It is usually quoted at around 300 metres; measured figures run nearer 220 metres. Wikipedia and most guides say 300 metres, and Visit Abu Dhabi says over 300 metres. PeakVisor lists 223 metres above sea level with 109 metres of prominence, and one Tripadvisor reviewer measured 209 metres on Google Earth. No official survey is published.
Wikipedia and Visit Abu Dhabi give 50 degrees, which Wikipedia describes as the slipface, the steep side of the dune. The dune is reported to be about 1,600 metres long.

faqs.q: How far is Moreeb Dune from Abu Dhabi and Dubai?
faqs.a: The official festival site says Liwa is about 3 hours from Abu Dhabi, and Wikipedia gives about 250km to the dune; other guides say 220km. For Dubai, guides give about 3.5 to 4 hours and one says about 350km. No official Dubai figure was found.

faqs.q: Can I drive to the base in a normal car?
faqs.a: Yes, according to the Desert Safaris Booking guide and the official site: a paved, double-lane road is reported to run to the dune's base and the festival site. One reviewer notes that sand sometimes covers parts of the tarmac.

faqs.q: Do I need a 4x4 for the sand?
faqs.a: To drive on the dune, yes. The official site recommends a 4x4 for dune exploration, and the Desert Safaris Booking guide lists a 4x4 with an experienced driver as one way up. Walking up needs no vehicle, though one guide says it takes 30 to 60 minutes and is physically demanding.

faqs.q: When is the Moreeb Dune hill climb?
faqs.a: It is part of the Liwa International Festival. In 2025–26 the festival ran from 12 December 2025 to 3 January 2026, and Gulf News gave 31 December 2025 to 3 January 2026 for the Moreeb Dune Car Championship. The 2026–27 festival runs from 11 December 2026 to 2 January 2027 according to the official site and Khaleej Times (checked 1 October 2026); specific hill-climb dates had not been published.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to visit Moreeb Dune?
faqs.a: The official festival site says general admission to the festival grounds is free, with separate fees for some competitions and VIP areas, shown on the Liwa Sports Club app. No fee for the dune itself outside the festival was found.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit, and how hot is it?
faqs.a: October to April, according to the official site. The site warns of extreme daytime heat and cold nights, and one booking-site guide says the sand holds heat by midday; go early with plenty of water, a hat and closed shoes.

seoTitle: Moreeb Dune, Liwa: Height, Road, Hill Climb & 4x4
seoDesc: Moreeb Dune (Tal Moreeb) in Liwa: reported height and slope, the drive from Abu Dhabi and Dubai, the paved road, the hill climb, 4x4 and heat advice.

productLink.sentence: The dune ridges drawn on {{link}} come from Liwa, at the edge of the Empty Quarter, the same landscape that Moreeb Dune rises from.

_doubts: HEIGHT: Wikipedia, Visit Abu Dhabi ('over 300 metres'), Gulf News ('over 300 meters') and several tour sites say about 300 m; PeakVisor lists 223 m above sea level with 109 m prominence (a different measure, elevation not dune height); one Tripadvisor reviewer says 209 m on Google Earth and 'nowhere near 300m'. No survey or official measurement was found. The text calls 300 m the 'commonly reported figure'. Visit Abu Dhabi's 'considered by many to be the world's tallest sand dune' and Wikipedia's 'tallest dune in the UAE' were not repeated as fact.

SLOPE: 50 degrees is from Wikipedia ('slipface'), Visit Abu Dhabi ('incline') and tour sites and blogs; no measurement source was found. The text says it is the slipface, not the whole climb. Length 1,600 m is Wikipedia and one booking site (Desert Safaris Booking) only.

DISTANCE FROM ABU DHABI: official festival site says 'just 3 hours'; Wikipedia says about 250 km to the dune; Gulf News, Nightdrive and an Abu Dhabi tour guide say about 220 km (Nightdrive says about 2 hours); Liwa Safari (not cited) says 4.5 hours and 220 km, which looks like an outlier. Route: the official site says E10 towards Sweihan and Al Ain; other guides say E11 and E45 via Madinat Zayed. The page gives 'about 3 hours', a distance range and both routes. Not confirmed with a map.

DISTANCE FROM DUBAI: no official figure. Nightdrive says about 3.5 hours; Vootours (not cited) says about 4 hours; Ghost Around the Globe says about 350 km; Liwa Safari (not cited) says 280+ km and 5+ hours. Only the 3.5 to 4 hour range and the 350 km figure are used, attributed to guides.

ROAD AND 4x4 CONFLICT: Desert Safaris Booking, Tripadvisor reviewers, Ghost Around the Globe and Nightdrive say the road is paved to the base and a 4x4 is not needed to reach it; the official site says main landmarks are reachable by paved road and a 4x4 is recommended for dune exploration. Vootours (not cited) says the route turns to unpaved desert tracks and a 4x4 is mandatory for the final stretch, which conflicts; the text follows the majority and the official site, and hedges. 'Access vehicle' is set to 2wd for reaching the base, with the 4x4 caveat in the note. The paved-to-base wording is from a tour-operator page (Desert Safaris Booking), not an official road source.

FESTIVAL DATES: official site and Khaleej Times say 12 Dec 2025 to 3 Jan 2026 for 2025-26, and for the next edition the official site main page, Khaleej Times and Nightdrive give 11 Dec 2026 to 2 Jan 2027 (the official site's page metadata still shows 3 Jan; corrected 1 Oct 2026). Hill-climb dates: Gulf News says the Moreeb Dune Car Championship ran 31 Dec 2025 to 3 Jan 2026; Liwa Safari (not cited) says 30 Dec to 3 Jan; the official FAQ mentions 29 to 31 December 2024 for an earlier year and gives no 2026-27 hill-climb dates; Visit Abu Dhabi says 'typically late December'. Wikipedia's mention of New Year's Eve fireworks was not repeated. Dates may have changed; confirm with the Liwa Sports Club app before publishing.

ENTRY FEE: the official site says general admission to the festival grounds is free with fees for some events. Liwa Safari (not cited) says Liwa Village has a separate ticket (15 to 30 AED); Emirates247 (not cited) says Liwa Village is free with some ticketed events. Not stated in the text. No fee for the dune outside the festival was found, so 'fees' says so rather than 'free'.

FACILITIES: toilets, park, car parks and playground come only from Tripadvisor reviewers, and cafeterias 'during events only'; they may be festival-only or out of date. Fuel: Liwa Safari (not cited) names an ADNOC station in Liwa City; Ghost Around the Globe names Madinat Zayed for supermarkets; no opened and cited source confirmed fuel at the base. Signal: the official site says generally available but may be weak in remote zones; Liwa Safari (not cited) says 5G towers at the festival. Shade is 'unknown'.

CAMPING: the official site names Liwa Sports Club for campsite booking, plus resorts and Bab Al Nojoum Camp glamping; Gulf News says the festival venue has designated camping sites. Ghost Around the Globe (one blog) says wild camping is permitted on an unpaved road, but no official statement of where wild camping is permitted was found, so it is only 'reported'. Phone numbers, prices (Liwa Safari says AED 500 to 1,000+ for pods) and the festival camping fees were not used.

DIFFICULTY: set to Moderate for the walk up the dune (Desert Safaris Booking says 30 to 60 minutes and physically demanding); driving the dune is a separate expert activity. This is a judgement; no source gave a rating.

HEAT/WEATHER: 22 to 30°C for October to April is one tour guide (Desert Safaris Booking); no meteorological record for the dune was opened. 'Sand burns bare feet' is from Ghost Around the Globe, 'holds heat by midday' from Desert Safaris Booking, 'hat by mid-morning' from one Tripadvisor reviewer. Best months: official site says October to April, Desert Safaris Booking says roughly the same, and Vootours (not cited) says November to March; the months array follows the existing Liwa page.

LOCATION WORDING: Wikipedia says the dune is about 25 km south of Liwa Oasis; the existing Liwa page says 25 km south of Mezairaa, and Visit Abu Dhabi gives 'Mahader Liwa'. Wikipedia's wording is used. The page does not use 'Mezairaa'.

GPS: Wikipedia's infobox coordinate (22.97966667, 53.78622222, read through the Wikipedia API; WebFetch of the page did not display it) is used. It matches Commons photo geotags within about 100 m but Wikipedia does not say whether it is the crest or the base. Third-party guides give 22.971, 53.774 (about 1.5 km away) and 22.9803, 53.7863 (PeakVisor); not used.

ARABIC NAME: 'تل مرعب' is from the Wikipedia lead, which gives the transliteration 'Mor'ib Hill'. The Commons page for one photo spells the name 'Tal Mor3ib' and the existing Liwa page uses 'Tal Mireb' and a Tripadvisor reviewer writes 'Tel Mireb'; spelling varies, so only Moreeb and Tal Moreeb are used in the text.

HERITAGE: the 2001 and 2004 history is from the Wikipedia festival page only; its organiser line ('Abu Dhabi Tourism Authority') conflicts with the 2026 organiser statement (Department of Culture and Tourism with Liwa Sports Club, per Khaleej Times), so only the 2004 motors club origin is used. A paved road built in 2004 (from Emirates247, not cited) was left out.

NOT FOUND: no official height or slope source, no official road source, no opening hours for the dune, no fee for the dune outside the festival, no camping rule for wild camping, no confirmed fuel station at the base, and no tour or recovery price. Not stated in the text.

SOURCES NOT CITED: pages opened but not used as citations because they were duplicative or conflicted: Vootours, Arabian Safari Royal, Abu Dhabi Desert Safari, Liwa Safari, Medium (Captain Dunes), Liwa Sports Club (lsc.ae), Abu Dhabi Media Office, Emirates247/EDC Tips. Time Out Abu Dhabi could not be fetched (405).

PHOTOS: Wikimedia Commons could not be opened with WebFetch ('cache-only' domain); the Commons API (curl) was used instead for search, categories, size, licence, author and geotags. The images themselves were not downloaded or viewed, so whether each 'clearly shows Moreeb Dune' rests on the title, category and geotag; a person should look before use. cover stays null.
